entries.description: Scientists have created one of the largest and most detailed simulations of the early universe ever made, offering an extraordinary new glimpse into the cosmos shortly after the Big Bang. Called Lumina, the groundbreaking simulation recreates the universe’s first 2 billion years, showing how dark matter, gas, and radiation interacted to give rise to the earliest stars, galaxies, and black holes.

entries.title: New 3D thermal invisibility cloak makes objects disappear from infrared cameras
entries.description: Researchers have developed a groundbreaking 3D invisibility cloak that can hide complex objects from infrared cameras while protecting them from extreme heat and cold. Instead of blocking heat, the device guides it around an object, making the object appear invisible to thermal imaging from virtually any direction. Successfully built and tested, the cloak could transform electronics cooling, thermal protection, and stealth technology.

entries.title: MIT scientists build a tiny robot that swims using living muscle cells
entries.description: MIT engineers have built a paper-thin swimming robot powered by living muscle cells that respond to flashes of light, allowing it to swim and steer through water. The breakthrough could pave the way for tiny, self-healing biological robots capable of exploring fragile environments that ordinary machines cannot safely navigate.

entries.title: Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist
entries.description: Cambridge researchers have created a groundbreaking $10 optical sensor that delivers the precision of laboratory equipment in a device small enough for wearable technology. It identified foods, plastics, and medicines with 100% accuracy in tests and demonstrated the ability to monitor blood glucose, alcohol, and other health markers without invasive procedures.

entries.title: A revolutionary new microscope could reveal the hidden machinery of life
entries.description: Researchers have developed a revolutionary microscope that uses an incredibly powerful laser to make previously invisible cellular structures easier to see. The technology dramatically improves image clarity, allowing scientists to examine small proteins that conventional electron microscopes struggle to capture. It could eventually reveal how tiny molecular machines interact inside cells, providing an unprecedented look at the hidden workings of life.

entries.title: Scientists reach the ultimate quantum limit on a surface
entries.description: Scientists have achieved a quantum breakthrough by creating an ultra-clean surface where individual molecules can maintain their delicate quantum properties at the fundamental limit. The discovery could unlock unprecedented control over molecules and help drive the next generation of quantum technologies.

entries.title: Astronomers uncover new secrets of the Universe’s first five minutes
entries.description: Scientists have achieved a major breakthrough in understanding the Universe’s earliest moments, measuring the amount of helium formed in the first five minutes after the Big Bang with unprecedented precision. Using one of the world’s most powerful telescopes, an international team studied 15 remarkably pristine galaxies that act as cosmic time capsules, preserving clues from nearly 13.8 billion years ago.

entries.title: Scientists who discovered a third form of magnetism win major physics prize
entries.description: Physicists have uncovered a hidden third form of magnetism that challenges more than 100 years of established physics. Called altermagnetism, the discovery could transform future computing and electronics while opening an entirely new frontier in quantum research.

entries.title: Astronomers discover a strange universal rule behind black hole eruptions
entries.description: Scientists have discovered that black holes of vastly different sizes appear to launch powerful jets according to the same universal rule. The breakthrough could explain why some black holes suddenly erupt years after devouring a star and help astronomers predict when these spectacular outbursts will happen.

entries.title: Scientists build a nuclear clock that could make atomic clocks obsolete
entries.description: Scientists in Vienna have achieved a major breakthrough in timekeeping by creating the world’s first self-stabilizing nuclear clock, a technology that could eventually surpass even the most precise atomic clocks. Instead of relying on electrons in atoms, the clock uses the tiny nuclei of thorium atoms, which are far less sensitive to outside disturbances.

entries.title: These spiders sleep like humans. But do they dream?
entries.description: Jumping spiders enter a REM-like state, darting their eyes and twitching their legs. What’s happening beyond that remains unclear

entries.title: Biologist David Sabatini wins $6 million in defamation lawsuit
entries.description: A jury ruled in favor of the former Whitehead Institute scientist, dismissing accuser’s claims of sexual harassment and retaliation

entries.title: NSF backs choice of new Antarctic contractor despite concerns by government watchdog and researchers
entries.description: Agency says it has “resolved” questions about KBR winning an $8 billion contract

entries.title: Two teams map development of mammal embryos, cell by cell
entries.description: Using genome editing to trace cell lineages, researchers capture the early history of the mouse embryo in unprecedented detail

entries.title: Possible plague death at a Siberian lab baffles scientists
entries.description: Much is unclear about the tragedy, but plague researchers say there is “zero” chance of an epidemic

entries.title: Five physics breakthroughs that should have won a Nobel Prize—but didn’t
entries.description: How politics, bad timing, and skepticism left foundation stones of modern physics unrecognized

entries.title: Scientists engineered a glowing cuttlefish. Why was it so hard?
entries.description: Breakthroughs in genetically altering cephalopods pave way for new studies of perception, brain evolution, and more

entries.title: NIH details $170 million biomedical research reproducibility effort
entries.description: Agency director announces literature search tool, other plans to improve reliability of science findings

entries.title: Capturing the complete process of embryonic development
entries.description: By tracking over 1 million cells, researchers created a detailed map of embryonic development in mice. It could provide development and disease insights.

entries.title: Seven MIT affiliates elected to the National Academy of Medicine for 2026
entries.description: Professor Michael Yaffe and six MIT alumni are honored for their outstanding professional achievement and commitment to service.

entries.title: A soft robot could help doctors diagnose and treat disorders of the small intestine
entries.description: MIT engineers designed a robotic enteroscope that can inch through the hard-to-reach small intestine, making biopsies and drug delivery easier.

entries.title: Learner collaborates with MIT peers to develop book of AI insights
entries.description: Prabha Jha used her experience with MIT Open Learning’s program for senior executives to develop AI solutions for her employer, Verizon, and to write a book.

entries.title: J-PAL North America launches Homelessness Evaluation Resource Hub to drive evidence-informed approaches to housing stability
entries.description: The hub serves as a free, online repository of essential content for policymakers, practitioners, and researchers seeking to leverage rigorous research to inform their approaches to homelessness.

entries.title: Startup plans to rejuvenate the nuclear power industry with a new manufacturing approach
entries.description: Founded by Jake Jurewicz ’14, SM ’15, Blue Energy manufactures giant pieces of nuclear reactors at shipyards and ships them on barges for final assembly, to lower costs.

entries.title: Beaver Works Summer Institute: A leader in transformational STEM education
entries.description: Jointly run by Lincoln Laboratory and the School of Engineering, the program has guided thousands of high school students to technical paths over the past 10 years.

entries.title: First Light: Celebrate the Inauguration of Caltech's 10th President, Ray Jayawardhana
entries.description: First light is the threshold moment in astronomy when a telescope makes its first observation and opens a new window to discovery. That same spirit of possibility defines the Caltech community. Through curiosity-driven inquiry, powerful experimentation, and groundbreaking instrumentation, Caltech illuminates new fields of knowledge and accelerates breakthroughs that shape the future of science, technology, and society.This fall, Caltech celebrates the spirit of first light for the Inauguration of Ray Jayawardhana as the Institute's 10th president. Over two days—Wednesday, October 28, and Thurs

entries.title: Caltech Mourns the Passing of Ted Scudder, 1930–2026
entries.description: Thayer (Ted) Scudder, Caltech's only professor of anthropology for the latter half of the 20th century, passed away October 22 at the age of 96. He was regarded as a leading specialist on dams and their lasting effects on communities and global ecosystems."Ted will be remembered as a world expert on the subject of forced population resettlement due to the construction of large dam projects," says economic anthropologist Jean Ensminger, Caltech's Edie and Lew Wasserman Professor of Social Sciences, Emeritus. entries.title: ‘Rocket revolution’ opens access to space
entries.description: For a long time, launching something beyond Earth was reserved for a relatively small number of national space programmes. That is changing.

entries.title: Beyond the Moon: Space Week around the world
entries.description: Right after the Soviet Union launched Sputnik in 1957, UNOOSA, the UN Office for Outer Space Affairs, was established and has since been monitoring developments across more than 77 successful lunar missions and other journeys while also taking a lead role in the annual World Space Week, which runs from 4 to 10 October.

entries.title: UN panel calls for stronger safeguards as AI agents advance
entries.description: The world's first scientific body on Artificial Intelligence called on Monday for AI safeguards to be adapted as current firewalls are “unravelling”.

entries.title: ADB Approves $100 Million Loan to Boost Skills Development and Jobs for Youth in Sri Lanka
entries.description: ADB has approved a $100 million results-based loan to help Sri Lanka transform its technical and vocational education and training system, equip more young people with industry-relevant skills, and strengthen the country's competitiveness and inclusive growth.

entries.title: ADB Advances Resilient Agriculture and Women's Economic Empowerment in Rural Cambodia
entries.description: ADB has approved a $72 million financing package to help Cambodia strengthen rural farming and increase women’s participation in agriculture, while enhancing the resilience of about 200,000 smallholder farmers in disaster-prone communes.

entries.title: ADB Launches $6 Billion Push for Healthier Seas and Coastal Economies
entries.description: ADB has announced it will mobilize up to $6 billion through 2030 to confront the mounting threats facing Southeast Asia’s seas and strengthen the blue economy that the region’s food supplies, jobs, and trade depend on.

entries.title: ADB Accelerates Nature Finance at COP17 with New Bond, Incubator, and Tracking Report
entries.description: ADB has announced a major push to expand financing for nature conservation and restoration, launching a new biodiversity bond, an investment incubator, and a joint multilateral development bank report to strengthen tracking of nature finance.

entries.title: ADB, Bank Respublika to Boost Access to Finance for Women-Led MSMEs and Agriculture Sector in Azerbaijan
entries.description: ADB and Bank Respublika Open Joint Stock Company have signed a $40 million loan to expand access to finance for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and agriculture borrowers in regions outside Azerbaijan’s capital, Baku.

entries.title: ADB Approves $100 Million Program to Strengthen Social Protection and Expand Economic Opportunities in Sri Lanka
entries.description: ADB has approved $100 million in financing to support reforms and investments that will strengthen social protection, economic inclusion, and well-being and resilience among the poor and elderly in Sri Lanka.

entries.title: ADB Approves $17.4 Million to Protect Bhutan Families from Middle East Impacts
entries.description: ADB has approved $17.42 million to help Bhutan protect vulnerable families from rising food and energy costs and maintain essential public services as the Middle East conflict puts pressure on the country’s economy.

entries.title: MDB Heads Strengthen Joint Action in Manila to Deliver More Financing and Greater Impact
entries.description: The Heads of Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs) Group met at the ADB headquarters in Manila to discuss how to deliver more financing and greater impact to support developing members as they face mounting challenges. It was the Group’s first-ever meeting in the Philippines, hosted by ADB as its 2026 Chair.

entries.title: ADB Approves $302 Million Loan to Modernize Baku Metro Signaling and Digital Operations
entries.description: ADB has approved a $302.38 million loan to modernize Baku Metro’s signaling system and digitalize its operations, helping to make metro services in Azerbaijan’s capital safer, more reliable, and more efficient while supporting the effective operation of its expanding network.

entries.title: ADB, Uzbekistan Sign $200 Million Power Modernization Loan
entries.description: ADB President Masato Kanda met Uzbekistan Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economy and Finance Jamshid Kuchkarov today and signed a $200 million loan agreement to modernize the country’s electricity distribution system, cut power losses, and improve reliability as electricity demand rises.

entries.title: ADB President Meets Thai Finance Minister, Marks $212 Million in ADB Financing for Hospitals Project
entries.description: ADB President Masato Kanda met Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas before joining him at a ceremony marking $212 million in ADB financing for a project to upgrade five public hospitals and improve access to specialist medical care for about 14 million people outside Bangkok.

entries.title: ADB Supports Modernization of Azerbaijan’s Bilajari–Yalama Railway Line
entries.description: ADB has approved a $350 million loan to install modern electrification, signaling, and telecommunication systems along the 192-kilometer double-track railway line between Bilajari and Yalama.

entries.title: ADB Approves $400 Million Loan to Support Earthquake Recovery, Expand SME Access to Finance in Türkiye
entries.description: ADB has approved a $400 million loan to Türkiye Vakıflar Bankası T.A.O. to support Türkiye’s post-earthquake recovery by building disaster-resilient houses, promoting clean energy, and expanding access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises owned by or employing women in less developed provinces.

entries.title: ADB Approves $100 Million Loan to Expand Access to Affordable, Resilient Housing Finance in Bangladesh
entries.description: ADB has approved a $100 million concessional loan to expand access to affordable and resilient housing finance for low- and middle-income borrowers in Bangladesh, particularly women.

entries.title: ADB Supports Fiscal Reforms for Stronger Public Service Delivery in Indonesia
entries.description: ADB has approved a $650 million equivalent program to help Indonesia modernize intergovernmental fiscal management, advance digital governance, and improve public service delivery across the country’s decentralized system of government.

entries.title: Four in five domestic workers lack formal job protections, UN finds
entries.description: An estimated 66.5 million domestic workers – representing more than four out of five domestic workers worldwide – were informally employed in 2025, a new report by the UN’s labour organisation has found.

entries.title: Soil mapping aims to boost agricultural production in Kenya
entries.description: A new Kenyan initiative is helping farmers better understand their soils in a bid to improve crop yields amid intensifying climate shocks.

entries.title: 800 million young people face a future without jobs
entries.description: Approximately 800 million young people entering the labour market in developing economies over the coming years will not find jobs unless countries act, the head of the UN Development Programme (UNDP) warned on Tuesday, as the agency launched two initiatives to boost investment and employment.

entries.title: Rise in poverty is ‘a wake-up call for the world’, UN development chief says
entries.description: The number of people living in “multidimensional” poverty has risen for the first time in 15 years, reaching 1.2 billion, as families struggle to meet their basic needs.

entries.title: ADB Launches New Approach to Build Resilience in Small Pacific Economies
entries.description: ADB has launched a new five-year strategy to strengthen resilience and expand economic opportunities in 12 Pacific island countries.

entries.title: ADB, Japan Back One of World’s Largest Green Ammonia Plants in First ACCEL Investment
entries.description: ADB and the Government of Japan have approved financing to AM Green Ammonia (India) Private Limited to help build one of the world’s largest plants to make ammonia using renewable energy in India, marking the first investment under the Action for Creating Energy Security for Long-term Resilience (ACCEL).

entries.title: ADB Evaluation Calls for Stronger Evidence of Development Impact from Private Equity Funds
entries.description: An evaluation by the Independent Evaluation Department of ADB finds that ADB's private equity fund investments remain a relevant instrument for mobilizing private capital and supporting private sector development, but the report calls for a clearer strategic framework, stronger articulation of ADB's additionality, and more consistent evidence of results.

entries.title: ADB President Calls for Greater Investment in Science, Energy, and AI
entries.description: ADB President Masato Kanda called for greater investment in scientific research and the infrastructure needed to turn discoveries into practical gains for people, pointing to ADB’s $50 billion Pan-Asia Power Grid Initiative and $20 billion Asia-Pacific Digital Highway as examples of the infrastructure investment already under way.

entries.title: ADB Supports Asia and Pacific’s First Sovereign Nature-Linked Bond in Thailand
entries.description: ADB has supported the Government of Thailand in issuing Asia and the Pacific’s first sovereign sustainability-linked bond incorporating a nature-related indicator, a significant milestone linking public sector financing with biodiversity outcomes.

entries.title: ADB, Naoero Airlines Sign Financing to Strengthen Air Connectivity in the Pacific
entries.description: ADB has signed a $15 million financing package with Nauru 40997 Leasing Corporation, a wholly owned subsidiary of Naoero Air Corporation, to improve transport resilience, regional connectivity, and cross-border trade and supply activities in Naoero and other remote and underserved Pacific island countries.

entries.title: Right to development: A blueprint for unmet promises
entries.description: Ahead of the 40th anniversary of the groundbreaking Declaration on the Right to Development this December, world leaders gathered at a High-Level Week meeting on Wednesday to map progress made and the 21st century challenges still ahead – from narrowing the digital divide to levelling the AI playing field – as the UN chief presented a “blueprint” to address promises that remain unfulfilled.

entries.title: ADB’s First Country Director for Türkiye Takes Up Post in Ankara
entries.description: ADB has appointed Keiju Mitsuhashi as its first Country Director for Türkiye, strengthening the bank’s presence on the ground as it expands its operations in the country.

entries.title: ADB, Credo Sign Local Currency Loan to Boost Financial Inclusion for MSMEs in Georgia
entries.description: ADB has signed a GEL120 million (approximately $44.5 million) local currency loan with JSC Credo Bank to help expand financing for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), including women MSMEs, operating in regions outside Tbilisi.

entries.title: CAREC Marks 25 Years with Over $60 Billion in Investment
entries.description: The Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) Program marked its 25th anniversary today with $60.2 billion in cumulative investment, having grown from five founding countries into an 11-country partnership.

entries.title: ADB Strengthens Regional Cooperation with New Malaysia Office
entries.description: ADB will strengthen its promotion of regional cooperation and integration, including support for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations Power Grid, by establishing a new office in Malaysia.

entries.title: ADB Sells $5 Billion Dual-Tranche 3- and 7-Year Global Benchmark Bonds
entries.description: ADB has priced a 3-year global benchmark United States dollar bond worth $3 billion and a 7-year global benchmark US dollar bond worth $2 billion, proceeds of which will become part of ADB’s ordinary capital resources.

entries.title: ADB Signs Private Sector Deal to Strengthen Mongolia's Cashmere Value Chain, Create Inclusive Jobs
entries.description: ADB has signed a combined $30 million loan (in togrog equivalent) with Gobi Joint Stock Company (Gobi), Tavan Bogd Foods LLC (TBF), and Tavan Bogd Foods Pizza LLC (TBFP) to strengthen Mongolia's cashmere value chain and expand employment opportunities in the country’s burgeoning food service sector.

entries.title: Clean your plate – to reduce food loss and waste
entries.description: Food waste is helping to fuel global warming, one half-eaten sandwich at a time.

entries.title: ADB Joins Effort to Advance Lower East Chao Phraya Initiative for Improved Flood Resilience in Thailand
entries.description: ADB joined development partners in support of the Lower East Chao Phraya Flood Management masterplan, a major effort led by the Government of Thailand to strengthen flood risk management, resilience, and sustainable water resources management.

entries.title: ADB President Joins Pre-COP31, Calls for Faster Resilience Finance
entries.description: ADB President Masato Kanda attended Pre-COP31 in Fiji and Tuvalu, where he met Fiji Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka and Tuvalu Prime Minister Feleti Teo and many other leaders, and called for faster financing to protect vulnerable island states from rising seas and other worsening impacts.

entries.title: ADB Launches New Country Partnership Strategy to Support Growth in Papua New Guinea
entries.description: ADB has launched a new 5-year country partnership strategy for Papua New Guinea to support stronger public finances, wider transport and energy connections, and better access to health, education, and other essential services.

entries.title: ADB, Modern Syntex Sign $50 Million Loan to Expand Energy-Efficient Polyester Chips Production in Bangladesh
entries.description: ADB and Modern Syntex Limited have signed a $50 million loan for the Modern Energy-Efficient Polyester Chips Manufacturing Project in Bangladesh.

entries.title: ADB’s New Maldives Strategy Prioritizes Fiscal Sustainability, Energy Security, and Climate Resilience
entries.description: ADB has endorsed its new country partnership strategy for Maldives, 2027–2031, to support the country’s efforts to strengthen fiscal sustainability, enhance energy security, and build resilience to natural hazards.

entries.title: UN human rights chief urges better protection of civilians in conflicts
entries.description: Youth-led protests against corruption and inequality in Serbia, Bangladesh, Nepal and Madagascar reflect a growing demand for reinforcing human rights around the world, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said at a press briefing on Wednesday.

entries.title: Protecting the storytellers: Women journalists on the frontline of conflict
entries.description: As online abuse, gender-based attacks and impunity ramp up the threats to women reporting from crisis zones, journalists and UN leaders are calling for urgent action to protect those who document conflict.

entries.title: World News in Brief: ‘No safe place in Ukraine’, IAEA calls for Iran nuclear inspections, Kenya hosts thousands of Ethiopians fleeing clashes
entries.description: The UN refugee agency (UNHCR) on Tuesday urged continued international support for Ukraine’s population as Russian airstrikes intensify and humanitarian needs grow in advance of another bitterly cold winter.

entries.description: The international community must combat inequality and stop wars from expanding to ensure a safer world for all, the UN Secretary-General said on Thursday.

entries.title: Gaza: Funding cuts leave half a million without food assistance
entries.description: Funding shortages have forced the World Food Programme (WFP) to slash assistance to hungry families in the Gaza Strip by roughly one third – a move that will affect some 500,000 people as winter approaches, the UN agency announced on Monday.

entries.title: Darfur: Healthcare needs outstrip resources as Security Council extends Sudan sanctions
entries.description: More than 700,000 displaced people in Tawila, in Sudan’s war-ravaged Darfur region, face severe shortages of healthcare, food, water and protection, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Thursday as it called for an urgent increase in resources.

entries.title: Ukraine: UN condemns latest attacks and calls for civilian protection
entries.description: The UN Humanitarian Coordinator for Ukraine on Wednesday called for an end to attacks against civilians following further overnight strikes by Russian forces that reportedly killed at least 19 in the Chernihiv Region.

entries.title: World News in Brief: Cycle of violence continues in Haiti, seafarer deaths off Somalia, food insecurity in the Middle East
entries.description: Haitians remain in the grip of lethal gang violence as it continues to “adapt and expand”, the UN’s top rights official, Volker Türk, said on Friday.

entries.title: World News in Brief: Storm clouds over Gaza, deadly obstacles face Mexican women rights defenders, Latvia booze ban proves lifesaver
entries.description: UN teams are racing to protect families in Gaza from the coming rainy season, but restricted access to land and shortages of critical supplies are hampering the effort, UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Wednesday.

entries.title: Security Council LIVE: Ambassadors meet as West Bank tensions rise, Gaza plan stalls
entries.description: The Security Council met Monday morning with prospects for peace in the Middle East under strain on two fronts. In the West Bank, settler violence and settlement expansion are raising fears for a two-State solution. In Gaza, a year-old peace plan has stalled while civilian suffering continues. The meeting comes as the plan’s remaining phases, including Hamas’ disarmament and Israel’s full withdrawal, remain unimplemented, and as the illegality of settlements under international law remains a key point of contention.

entries.title: Sentinel-3C returns its first views of Earth
entries.description: Just two weeks after it was launched, the Copernicus Sentinel-3C satellite returned its first images and measurements from two of its key instruments – a major milestone that confirms the satellite is working well and on the road to monitoring the health of Earth’s oceans, land, cryosphere and atmosphere.

entries.title: FLEX and Sentinel-3C launched
entries.description: The European Space Agency’s FLEX Earth Explorer satellite and the Copernicus Sentinel-3C satellite have been launched together aboard a Vega-C rocket from Europe’s Spaceport in French Guiana, marking a new milestone in Europe’s Earth Observation Programmes.

entries.title: Nuclear-powered spaceships
entries.description: Just before the Artemis II crew began its historic slingshot around the moon this past April, NASA announced plans to build Space Reactor-1 Freedom. SR-1, the first-ever nuclear-reactor-­powered interplanetary spacecraft, is meant to fly an uncrewed mission to Mars by the end of 2028, arriving in 2029. entries.title: NASA astronauts splash down after 100 million miles in space
entries.description: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 astronauts have returned to Earth after 237 days in space, traveling more than 100 million miles and completing over 3,792 orbits while conducting research to prepare for future missions to the Moon and Mars. The mission also made history with record-setting spacewalk achievements and experiments that could transform medicine both in space and on Earth.

entries.title: Untied Launch Alliance announces mid-November return to flight for Vulcan rocket
entries.description: The anticipated launch will be the first for the heavy-lift rocket since a mid-flight nozzle failure on a solid rocket booster. The rocket will carry 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit.
